Description
Since its introduction in 1979, the Canadian Maple Leaf Gold coin has sold over 25 million troy ounces, making it one of the most popular
gold bullion coins
in the world. The Canadian Maple Leaf 1/20 oz Gold Coin of .9999 fine gold is a charm for small investors who are new to the precious metal investment market.
1/20 oz Gold Maple Leaf coins are a great way to invest in Gold and many consider the Maple Leaf to be one of the world’s most beautiful gold coins. These 1/20 oz gold coins come from the prestigious precious metal refiner Royal Canadian Mint.
Each Canadian Maple Leaf Gold coin is a legal Canadian Gold tender guaranteed by the Government of Canada for its weight and purity. At up to .9999-fine pure Gold, the Maple Leaf bullion coins are some of the world’s premier Gold bullion coins. Investing in Canadian 1/20 oz gold coins is a great way to get very high-quality gold for a fraction of the cost.
Design of Canadian Maple Leaf 1/20 oz Gold Coin
Every coin has a good design and a good value. The Canadian Maple Leaf Gold coin is beautifully crafted and elaborately designed.
Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II is depicted on the obverse side of the 1/20 oz Gold Canadian Maple Leaf Coin. Because Queen Elizabeth II is the monarch of the Commonwealth of Nations, she is featured prominently on the faces of several currency coins. On the obverse, you can see the coin value and the year it was produced, as well as the noble Queen Elizabeth II.
The distinctive
sugar maple leaf
is depicted on the reverse side of the Candian Maple Leaf 1/20 oz Gold  Coin, along with engravings indicating the country of issue, the coin’s purity, metal content, and weight.
Main Highlights of 1/20 oz Gold Coin – Canadian Maple Leaf
Contains 1/20 troy oz of .9999 fine gold
Manufactured by the Royal Canadian Mint.
Bears a face value of $1 backed by the federal government in Canada.
The obverse features her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II along with the face value and coin year.
The reverse features the depiction of the distinctive maple leaf along with the nation of issue, purity, metal content, and weight of the silver coin.
